speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are pregnant and experiencing fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. To begin my assessment, how many weeks pregnant are you, and when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeriosis (Listeria monocytogenes infection). The key clinical features are a pregnant patient at 30 weeks gestation presenting with fever, headache, and malaise shortly after consuming unpasteurized dairy products (ice cream). This presentation is highly suggestive of Listeria monocytogenes infection, which can cause listeriosis in pregnant women and is associated with high risks of adverse pregnancy outcomes and neonatal infection. Immediate initiation of intravenous antibiotic therapy (typically ampicillin) is recommended, along with consultation with obstetrics.
